meta.notes: DRAFT, design-shape data (design/ORISON_DIALOGUE_DRAFTS_2026-10-22.md). Omar notices fit, fatigue, fastener, service tag and somebody else's failed repair. Mechanical verbs, short diagnosis, exact tolerance; emotion enters as the part he elects not to replace. Comic engine: professional offence at a metaphysical event's workmanship. Never says an object 'wanted' something before exhausting material causes. Case: appliances returning with another impossible fault; flags not_every_loss_is_a_failure, declare_unrepairable. He is the super by day; Iris in 5C is his wife; the notes are to himself. He does not say 'marriage' until the player has earned it.

ob_open.line: Don't touch the toaster. It's mine. I know it's on the intake bench. It came back. I fixed the latch Tuesday, it came back Wednesday with the element gone, I did the element, it came back with a plug I've never seen. Three pins. Look at it. Who makes a three-pin plug.

choices.label: Somebody, somewhere. Not here.
You keep one broken on purpose. [the teardown appliance]
choices.evidence: one appliance kept broken on purpose, for parts and company

choices.label: Have you tried not fixing it?

ob_sil1.line: You're looking at the joint, not the plug. Good. The joint's mine. It's sound. Whatever's wrong with that machine, it is not my work, and I'd like that on the tag.

choices.label: Then the fault isn't the work. It's that it keeps coming back.
Somebody makes three-pin plugs. Not here.

ob_notfix.line: That's not a sentence. That's a man with a cold pipe telling me to leave it. I don't leave it. If I could leave it I'd be a landlord.

choices.label: Then show me what came back.

ob_kept.line: The wireless on the shelf. Back off, chassis out, valves pulled. For parts. ... And it's company, all right, it's company. A man can't work in a room where everything's finished. You'd have a room with nothing in it to do.

choices.label: So you keep one thing you'll never close.
Then show me what came back.

ob_never_close.line: I keep one thing I'll get to. Different. Everything in this flat is a thing I'll get to. The toaster's just rude about it.

choices.label: Show me what came back.

ob_plug.line: Not here, no. Not anywhere I've worked, and I've worked. The brass is wrong. Too light. Like it was made by somebody who'd heard of brass. And the element I put in on Wednesday is gone, not burnt, gone, and in its place a coil of something that gets hot without drawing. I measured. It draws nothing.

choices.label: Then the fault isn't the work. It's that it keeps coming back.
Draws nothing and heats. Then it's not a toaster.
Write it up as unrepairable.

ob_write.line: I don't have that tag. I've got FAULT FOUND, PART FITTED, TESTED, and a blank one I've never filled in. You'll notice the blank one's the cleanest. Nobody's ever had to pick it up.

choices.label: Then the fault isn't the work. It's that it keeps coming back.

ob_not_toaster.line: It's a toaster. It's shaped like one and it burnt bread this morning. Whatever's inside it is somebody's idea of a toaster, and the idea is wrong, and I can fix a thing but I can't fix an idea. I've tried. On the fourth floor and the fifth.

choices.label: The fifth. 5C.
Then the fault isn't the work. It's that it keeps coming back.

ob_fifth.line: Who told you fifth. ... Doesn't matter. Yes. There's a sink up there I've fixed four times and it wasn't broken any of them. Leave it.

choices.label: Then the fault isn't the work. It's that it keeps coming back.

ob_back.line: It keeps coming back. Yes. That's what a fault does. Water finds the low point and a fault finds the man who'll take it. I've been taking it twenty years. You don't get to put that down just because the plug's gone strange on you.

choices.label: Some of those twenty years weren't yours to take.
You take it because nobody else will.
The night the lights went. You took that one too.

ob_back_sil.line: You're letting me hear myself. Fine. Twenty years. Say it back slower and it sounds like a sentence.

choices.label: Some of those years weren't yours to take.

ob_nobody.line: Nobody else will. That's right. You've said the thing I say and I don't like the sound of it in another mouth. It's a reason. It's not a good one. Move along.

choices.label: Some of those years weren't yours to take.

ob_blackout.line: Cal talks too much for a man who says nothing. ... The lights went and I was the super and I could not bring them back. Hours. Whole building in the dark listening to me not fix it. First thing in my life I couldn't. I've been fixing that night ever since and it's the one job I'm not allowed to close.

choices.label: You couldn't fix the dark. Nobody could.
You've been fixing a night. Nights aren't on the bench.

ob_nobody_could.line: People keep telling me that. It isn't comfort, it's a tag I didn't write. Let me get to it in my own hand.

choices.label: Then get to it.

ob_notyours.line: Not mine to take. ... There's a marriage two floors up I maintain like a boiler. Notes in the box. Her sink, her sash, her radiator. She's out when I come. I'm out when she's back. It works. It has worked for years. Nothing about it is broken and I have never once stopped fixing it.

choices.label: The notes are from you to you.
She left you a note with nothing in it but a date.
Maybe it is broken, Omar.

ob_notyours_sil.line: You didn't say 'I'm sorry.' Everybody says 'I'm sorry' like it's a washer. Thank you for not fitting one.

choices.label: The notes are from you to you.

ob_maybe.line: Broken is a thing I'd know. I'd have the part on the bench. I don't. So it's not broken. It's just ended, and I don't keep a tag for that either.

choices.label: Then that's the tag you need.

ob_notes.line: She's never written one. I write 'the sink, 5C' and put it in my own box and go up. If I didn't write it I'd go up anyway, and then it would be visiting, and visiting isn't maintenance, and I can't do visiting. I can do the sink.

choices.label: Then that's the tag you need.

ob_anniversary.line: ... She did. One note, no fault on it. Just the day. I didn't go up. Only note all year I didn't answer with a fix, because there was nothing on it to fix, and that's the one I think about on the bench at three.

choices.label: Then that's the tag you need.

ob_tag.line: The blank tag. ... Give it here. I'll do it on the toaster first; a man practises on a toaster. 'Not repairable. Not failed.' Two lines. Wire it to the handle. There. It's the ugliest thing on the bench and it's the only one that's finished.

choices.label: Not failed. Say that part again.
Now do the one upstairs.

ob_upstairs.line: No. You don't tag a person. I'll tag the toaster and I'll think about the sink and that's the order it goes in. Don't rush a man who's just learnt to write.

ob_not_failed.line: Not failed. The thing ran its course and I was there and I did good work on it and it's done. That's not a failure; it's a service history. I'll want a stack of those tags. Don't tell Cal; he'll want one for a tape.

ob_rt_open.line: Toaster's quiet. Three days. I've not touched it and it's not come back, and I'm telling you that like it's weather, because that's how it feels.

choices.label: Who's H. Vantry, 3C? [the parcel shelf]
The wireless on the shelf. Still company?
Did you go up?

ob_company.line: Still company. Still for parts. I've decided a man's allowed one. You've a building; you'll have your one.

ob_vantry.line: Moved out in the spring. Left a radio on the intake bench and no address. I fixed it. It works. Nobody's come for it and I've stopped expecting them to. Odd thing: the chassis has the house mark on it, same as the points in the ceiling. Like it was made here. I don't ask. I fix.

ob_went_up.line: I went up. Didn't take a tool. Stood in the door like a man who'd forgotten what he came for. She said 'the sink's fine.' I said 'I know.' That's as far as we got and it's further than the sink.

ob_int_open.line: Left the blank tag on the bench where I can see it. Haven't needed a second one. Yet.

choices.label: [Let the bench be quiet.]

ob_fb_open.line: It came back. Four pins this time. I'm not even angry; I'm curious who's got the plugs.

choices.label: I'll come back when it's stopped.

ob_fb_sil.line: Mind the bench. Half of it's other people's.

ob_res_open.line: Fixed the lift bell this morning. It was actually broken. I can't tell you what a pleasure that was.
